dossier.public_summary: The dip is seen only in alternating eclipses and only in two sectors, with two extremely deep events driving the signal. A small star's eclipses blended in the aperture or a binary at half the reported period explains the pattern far better than a ~1.4 Earth-radius transiting planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even events have a 39x depth difference, only one class shows a ~800 ppm dip. This is positive evidence for an eclipsing binary at twice the period (27.2 d), not a planet at 13.6 d, with consistency across sectors (sector_oe_max_sigma 31.69, 2 sectors over 3).

Depth is not steady: sector 66 shows 1359 +/-77 ppm while sectors 13,39,93 show ~2-45 ppm consistent with noise. Changes within a single pipeline rule out a steady transiting planet and indicate a blend/sector-dependent EBs.

reasons.why: The signal is driven by two ~3000-4000 ppm outliers out of 11 transits; all other events are near zero. A planet must show ~300 ppm in every transit.

reasons.why: Independent classifier trained on followed-up signals rates this as planet-like as only the bottom ~7% of known planets; combined with the other positive EB signs it supports rejection.
